title: plotkit spec
description: What a model writes for plotkit: a curve (instrument export, x / y1 / y2) or a chart of table data (a "chart" key). Generated by python -m plotkit schema --json; do not edit.

color.description: a colour: a name (red, navy), a Korean name (빨강, 남색) or a hex code (#c0392b)

column.description: a column: its letter as in Excel ("B"; in text files A is the first field), its name, or part of its name

file.description: data file path, or a list of paths (xlsx/xls/csv/txt/...); * and ? patterns are expanded

sheets.description: "all", a sheet name, a 1-based sheet number, or a list of those

ask.description: the user's ask, in their words

header_row.description: 1-based row of the column names; normally automatic

data_start_row.description: 1-based first row of numbers; normally automatic

decimal.description: text files only: "." or ","; normally automatic

encoding.description: text files only, e.g. "utf-8", "cp949", "utf-16"; normally automatic

read.description: how to read the files; normally automatic

echarts.description: ECharts engine only: a partial ECharts option merged over the drawn plot, checked against an allowlist (title, legend, grid, xAxis, yAxis, series[i] styles and markArea/markLine/markPoint, graphic text/line/rect). series 0 = y1, 1 = y2 (combine: one y1 series per sheet, then one y2 series per sheet). Use only for things no key covers.

patch_value.description: a plain value: text, a number, a colour, or a list of those; no links, data URLs or functions

bins.description: histogram: number of bins, {"width": w}, or a list of edges; heatmap: bin a numeric x or y with x.bins

chart_axis.description: a chart axis: x, y or z

file.description: data file path, or a list of paths (xlsx/xls/csv/txt/...)

sheets.description: "all" (default), a sheet name, a 1-based sheet number, or a list of those

preset.description: "tga" (default; TGA labels, residue + DTG peak) or "none" (plain plot, you must give x.col and y1.col)

read.description: how to read the files; normally automatic

col.description: column letter like "B" (as in Excel; for text files A = 1st field) or part of the column name like "Temperature"

label.description: axis label text (default: the preset's label, or the column's name when its unit differs, e.g. Weight (mg))

min.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

max.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

step.description: distance between tick marks, e.g. 200 or 0.2

label_size.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

label_color.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

tick_size.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

tick_color.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

minor.description: true for minor ticks between the numbered ones

invert.description: true to reverse the axis (x: high temperature on the left); x.flip: true means the same

x.description: the x axis: a column, or an object

col.description: column letter like "B" (as in Excel; for text files A = 1st field) or part of the column name like "Temperature"

label.description: axis label text (default: the preset's label, or the column's name when its unit differs, e.g. Weight (mg))

min.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

max.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

step.description: distance between tick marks, e.g. 200 or 0.2

legend.description: name in the legend (default: the axis label)

label_size.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

label_color.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

tick_size.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

tick_color.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

minor.description: true for minor ticks between the numbered ones

invert.description: true to reverse the axis (x: high temperature on the left); x.flip: true means the same

y1.description: the y1 axis: a column, or an object

col.description: column letter like "B" (as in Excel; for text files A = 1st field) or part of the column name like "Temperature"

label.description: axis label text (default: the preset's label, or the column's name when its unit differs, e.g. Weight (mg))

min.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

max.description: axis range; leave out for automatic

step.description: distance between tick marks, e.g. 200 or 0.2

legend.description: name in the legend (default: the axis label)

label_size.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

label_color.description: font size / color of the axis label (y labels default to the line color)

tick_size.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

tick_color.description: font size / color of the tick numbers (y ticks default to the line color)

minor.description: true for minor ticks between the numbered ones

invert.description: true to reverse the axis (x: high temperature on the left); x.flip: true means the same

y2.description: false to draw no second axis

count.description: peak: how many peaks to label (default 1)

min_rel.description: peak: extra peaks must be at least this fraction of the main one (default 0.1)

text.description: label template: {x} {y} or {} (e.g. "Residue {}%", "{x:.0f} °C", "Residue {y:.2f}%"); the preset residue label uses the column's unit when it isn't %, e.g. "Residue 0.82 mg"

type.description: "value_at_x" | "peak" | "vline" | "hline" | "text" | "band" (guessed from the name: residue*/value* -> value_at_x, peak*/max* -> peak, band*/shade* -> band)

x.description: value_at_x / vline: the x position, e.g. 800

x_max.description: peak: only search in this x range; band: the shaded x range (both needed)

x_min.description: peak: only search in this x range; band: the shaded x range (both needed)

annotate.description: dict of labels; set one to false to remove a preset label (e.g. "peak": false), true to ask for a preset label as it is (e.g. "residue": true). A value_at_x label with no data at its x shows "no data" only when the spec names it; otherwise it is left out

title.description: plot title text, or {"text": ..., "size": ..., "color": ...}; "{sheet}" (default) and "{file}" are replaced; "" for none

legend.description: legend position "center left" (default), "best", "upper right", "lower left", ..., "none"; or {"where": ..., "show": true/false, "size": ...}

text_color.description: color of all text that has no color of its own (default black); when given, also the y-axis labels, tick labels and residue/peak labels, which otherwise follow the line colors

code.description: matplotlib engine only: extra Python run after drawing, before saving. Names: fig, ax1 (left y), ax2 (right y or None), x, y1, y2 (arrays), sheet, plt, np. Use only for things no key covers.

echarts.description: ECharts engine only: a partial ECharts option merged over the drawn plot, checked against an allowlist (title, legend, grid, xAxis, yAxis, series[i] styles and markArea/markLine/markPoint, graphic text/line/rect). series 0 = y1, 1 = y2 (combine: one y1 series per sheet, then one y2 series per sheet). Use only for things no key covers.

font.description: font family; Korean fonts are picked automatically when text is Korean

combine.description: true = all sheets in ONE figure (one color per sheet)

colors.description: combine: one colour per sheet or file, in order (a list), or "mono"

names.description: combine: the legend name of each sheet or file, in order (a list)

offset.description: combine: shift each next curve's y1 by this much (e.g. 20), so the curves do not overlap; labels keep the real values

panels.description: "split": y1 in an upper panel and y2 in a lower panel with the same x axis

data_code.description: Python run in a sandbox before drawing, per sheet: x, y1, y2 (numpy arrays), sheet, np; reassign them to change the curve; append {"type": "vline"|"hline"|"text", "x": .., "y": .., "text": ..} to marks

dir.description: output folder (default: <data file name>_plots next to the data)

name.description: file name template; default "{sheet}" ("{file}_{sheet}" for several files)

output.description: the files to write; the host's folder and formats win (plotkit.render)

curve.description: An instrument curve (TGA and other x-y exports): x, a left axis y1 and a right axis y2.

file.description: as in plotkit; with several sheets or files the rows are stacked and a column "sheet" / "file" says where each row came from (default: the first sheet)

asks.description: what the user asked, one entry per ask: [{"ask": "R3만", "how": "key"}, {"ask": "...", "how": "data_code" | "code" | "echarts" | "unsupported"}]; unsupported asks are reported to the user

bins.description: histogram: number of bins, {"width": w}, or a list of edges; heatmap: bin a numeric x or y with x.bins

by.description: column that splits the data into series (one colour each); grouped bars, or stacked with "stack": true

code.description: matplotlib only: Python after drawing (fig, ax, plt, np, data)

colors.description: list of colours, {"<series or category>": colour}, or "mono" for black and grey

corr.description: heatmap of correlations: a list of numeric columns, or "all"

data_code.description: Python run in a sandbox BEFORE filtering and drawing, on the pandas DataFrame df (also pd, np); change or add columns, e.g. "df['K'] = df['T'] + 273.15". Works on both engines.

density.description: histogram: true for density instead of counts

dpi.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

echarts.description: ECharts only: a partial option merged over the drawn chart

engine.description: "matplotlib" | "echarts": used only when the host does not choose the engine

error.description: bar: error bars from the rows of each bar: "std" | "sem" | "minmax"

filter.description: list of conditions: "반응기 == R3", "주차 >= 10", "촉매 로트 in [FC-2405, FC-2407]", "날짜 between 2024-03-01 and 2024-03-31", "등급 != 불합격", "비고 contains 노즐"

font.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

font_size.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

grid.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

highlight.description: a category (or list) drawn in colour, the rest grey

legend.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

notes.description: free text for the model's own notes; not drawn

output.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

percent.description: accepted but not drawn yet: percent-stacked bars have no key (mark such an ask unsupported)

read.description: as in plotkit; with several sheets or files the rows are stacked and a column "sheet" / "file" says where each row came from (default: the first sheet)

ref.description: reference lines: [{"y": 5.2, "text": "목표"}, {"y": "mean"}, {"x": 10}]; "mean"/"median" use all filtered rows

sheets.description: as in plotkit; with several sheets or files the rows are stacked and a column "sheet" / "file" says where each row came from (default: the first sheet)

size.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

smooth.description: moving average: N or {"window": N, "raw": true to keep the raw line}

sort.description: "desc" | "asc" (by value) | "x" (by category) | a list of categories; top: keep the N largest (pie: the rest go into "기타")

stack.description: bar / hbar / histogram: true stacks the series of "by" instead of setting them side by side

text_color.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

title.description: as in plotkit; legend where may also be "outside right" / "outside bottom"

top.description: "desc" | "asc" (by value) | "x" (by category) | a list of categories; top: keep the N largest (pie: the rest go into "기타")

trend.description: scatter: true for a straight-line fit per series ({"label": true} also writes the slope and R²)

values.description: true to write the value on bars / heatmap cells / pie slices, or a format like "{:.1f}" (pie: "percent" (default), "value", "both")

x.description: a column (name, part of a name, or letter) or {"col", "label", "min", "max", "step", "log", "flip", "rotate", "format", "order", "period", "bins", "date_format"}; y may be a list of columns (one series each)

y.description: a column (name, part of a name, or letter) or {"col", "label", "min", "max", "step", "log", "flip", "rotate", "format", "order", "period", "bins", "date_format"}; y may be a list of columns (one series each)

z.description: heatmap cell value: a column or {"col", "agg"} (default "count" of rows)

chart.description: A chart of table data (bar, hbar, line, scatter, histogram, heatmap, pie).
